card.summary: 'On the Free plan that means up to 25 GB of storage and 5 GB per file.' Remote upload 'is included on the Free plan', but 'An upload.am account' is required.

record.category: free cloud storage with server-side remote upload from a URL

free_tier.stated: 'On the Free plan that means up to 25 GB of storage and 5 GB per file.' Remote upload 'is included on the Free plan', but 'An upload.am account' is required.
free_tier.notes: The same page's feature blurb advertises '25 GB free forever' and 'No ads on download pages'.

per_object_cap.stated: 5 GB per file on the Free plan ('a file within your plan's size limit. On the Free plan that means up to 25 GB of storage and 5 GB per file').

retention.stated: unverified: the page describes expiry controls for links the user creates, but no default retention period for stored files.

egress.terms: No traffic allowance stated; files are served from the account's links with optional password, download limit and expiry.

record.interface_detail: Web cabinet only: paste an http(s) link, the server fetches it in the background, and the file appears in a folder where it can be previewed, renamed, shared or versioned. Private-range and credential-bearing URLs are refused.
record.tooling: Browser. No API is documented on the feature pages read, so a wrapper drives the cabinet.
record.chaining: It is the storage end of a relay: pull a direct link into a durable account and share it with controls the original host lacks. 25 GB fits a small working set, not the hot tier at 10 TiB.

limits.value: 25 GB stored on the Free plan
5 GB per file on the Free plan
an account is required; executable and script types are blocked

record.limits_note: The fetch only works on a direct link that needs no login on the source site; a host page with a download button is refused before the transfer starts.
record.binding_note: At 1 TiB/month the 25 GB storage allowance binds first and hard: the 5 GB per-file cap is generous relative to it, and deleting after download does not change the fact that the account holds 25 GB at a time.

identity_cost.detail: 'An upload.am account. Remote upload lives in the cabinet, so register for free if you have not already.' Registration was not attempted, so the fields are unverified beyond an account being required.

record.reliability_note: Remote fetch is asynchronous and failures arrive by email, so a wrapper cannot tell success from a silent queue. The service refuses private-network URLs and executable types, which will reject some legitimate archives.
record.confidence_note: The plan limits and the remote-upload mechanics are quoted from the vendor page; no fetch was executed, which a measured rung needs.

evidence.proved: 'On the Free plan that means up to 25 GB of storage and 5 GB per file'; remote upload included on Free; account required; direct-link-only and private-address refusal

record.notes: The clearest published free URL-pull-to-storage allowance found: 25 GB stored, 5 GB per file, account required, direct links only. Useful as a staging buffer, not as the 10 TiB tier.
